answer.generated: Two key design issues in distributed systems engineering are transparency and openness. Transparency concerns the extent to which the distributed system should appear as a single system to the user, determining when it is beneficial for users to be aware of the system's distributed nature. Openness involves whether the system should be designed using standard protocols that promote interoperability, or more specialized protocols that offer greater flexibility but may limit compatibility with other systems.
